newsitem.title: USA: US Airways to pare Baltimore flights, staff.
newsitem.headline: US Airways to pare Baltimore flights, staff.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc said Monday it will cut about 240 full-time and part-time customer service and maintenance workers in Baltimore.

The staff cuts come amid US Airways' plans to pare departures from Baltimore, while bolstering international operations in Philadelphia, spokesman Rick Weintraub said. An undetermined number of positions will be added in Philadelphia, he said.

The Arlington, Va.-based airline will drop flights from Baltimore to Louisville, Kentucky and Cleveland, Ohio. Flights to Buffalo, N.Y. and Rochester, N.Y. will be shifted to US Airways' express operation.
Certain flights from Baltimore to the Caribbean will be shifted to Philadelphia as US Airways tries to expand its international hub in Philadelphia, Weintraub said.
US Airways will add flights from Baltimore to San Francisco, Boston and Philadelphia.
US Airways, which has among the highest costs in the airline industry, has been reevaluating its route and hub structure.
The company is currently in labor talks with its pilots and its mulling plans to create a new, low-cost unit.
